scope: Isolated software inspection and refusing-upload fixtures only; source-bound to the snapshot above

observations.universal_stat_failure_refusal_exception: Metadata error suppression can omit a new untracked file from state_hash and accept an older matching receipt before size/auth checks.

findings.title: Failed metadata stat can leave an older receipt accepted for a new untracked file
findings.observation: A synthetic prior receipt for the same HEAD/RESUME without an untracked payload was retained. Adding a new payload and failing every stat call left the digest equal; the copied-script fixture gate returned 0 before sizing/authentication and called no upload stub. The existing receipt was unchanged and no new receipt was created.
findings.recommendation: Propagate metadata stat failures through state_hash and its callers before consulting cached receipts; cover this case with a refusing-upload fixture.
findings.limits: The prior receipt was seeded by the fixture; no authentic historical upload was reproduced. Parent revision was inspected, not executed.

findings.title: Committed regressions omit cached-receipt metadata-failure coverage
findings.observation: The four cases start without a prior receipt and do not compare successful state_hash contributions. Separate reviewer helper probes compare successful metadata/size exactly, but do not modify committed coverage.

                        'hash_returncode': current.returncode, 'hash_stderr': current.stderr,
                        'fixture_gate_returncode': call.returncode, 'fixture_gate_stdout': call.stdout,
                        'fixture_gate_stderr': call.stderr, 'receipt_unchanged': receipt.read_bytes() == receipt_bytes,
                        'upload_or_auth_command_called': network_log.exists(),
                        'new_receipt_created_by_script': False,
                        'finding_reproduced': current.returncode == 0 and current.stdout.strip() == initial_hash and call.returncode == 0 and receipt.read_bytes() == receipt_bytes and not network_log.exists()}
            assert observed['finding_reproduced'], observed
            print(json.dumps(observed, indent=2))
        finally:
            case.doCleanups()
    finally:
        os.environ.clear()
        os.environ.update(previous_env)
